subject: Post-demo: model-fit benchmarks, prompt sets, and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@clearsight.com>, Mike Johnson <mike.j@clearsight.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model-fit benchmarks, prompt sets, and next steps

Hi Sara / Mike —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

Summary of call
- Use case: assisted chart summarization + clinical note drafting for intake teams (short-form prompts, many turn-backs)
- Primary constraints: p95 latency target <= 250ms for the 90% of production traffic; cost sensitivity for lower-throughput hours; SOC2 + data residency checks in procurement.

Redwood-verified perf profiles (attached & linked)
- rw-instruct-13b-q4f (recommended for initial eval): sustained throughput ~140-160 TPS, p50 30ms, p95 110–140ms on g5d.48x with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled.
- rw-chat-7b-v2 (latency-first): sustained ~320 TPS, p50 12ms, p95 60–90ms (good for short-turn interactions).
- Notes: throughput above assumes typical prompt lengths (avg 160 tokens request / 100 tokens gen). We include token distribution histograms in the attached PDF.

Attachments & artifacts
- redwood_bench_20261108_summary.pdf (Redwood verified summary with per-model TPS and latency percentiles)
- clearsight_promptset_v1.txt (you shared during the call; I attached for reference)
- quick bench dashboard: https://bench.redwood.ai/reports/rdw-clrs-202611

Proposed next steps
1) Choose eval mode: 48-hour hosted smoke test (we run against your prompt set) OR 2-week dedicated trial on reserved capacity. Recommend 48-hour hosted to validate latency profile quickly.
2) Agree success criteria: p95 <= 250ms on the sampled prompt set AND generation quality A/B with your golden prompts (we'll set up simple side-by-side diffs).
3) Logistics: we need a contact for procurement + a sample S3/secure transfer for any PHI-mapped test data.

Can you confirm which eval mode you prefer and who from procurement should I loop in? I'll schedule the run once we agree.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_bench_20261108_summary.pdf (pdf)]
From: Sara Park <sara@clearsight.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-fit benchmarks, prompt sets, and next steps

Hey Rishi —

Appreciate the write-up. A few quick clarifying Qs before we lock in the 48-hour run: 
1) The p95 numbers you shared — are those cold-start inclusive (no warm KV cache) or warm?
2) Can you confirm whether the hosted eval can be done with our prompt set and masked PHI (we'll provide a masked sample)?
3) We will also need a ballpark for expected spend for a 48-hour hosted eval and any procurement paperwork.

I'll attach the current prompt set (sanitized) — please use that exact file for the run.

Thanks,
Sara
Lead Product Manager, ClearSight Health
sara@clearsight.com
[Attachment: clearsight_promptset_v1.txt (text)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@clearsight.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-fit benchmarks, prompt sets, and next steps

Sara —

Short answers:
- p95 in the attached summary is measured on a warm runtime with prefix/KV cache populated (representative of sustained service). Cold-starts without cache are ~2–3x higher at p95 depending on sequence length; we'll include a cold-start sweep if you want.
- Yes — we can run on your masked prompt set. For PHI-adjacent data we support secure transfer (S3 + KMS) or VPC peering in Private evals. For 48-hour hosted we'll use masked data you provide via a secure upload link.
- Ballpark: a 48-hour hosted smoke test (with 1 service worker) typically maps to $2.5k–$6k depending on gen size and concurrency; I can give a precise estimate after we pick the model variant and concurrency target.

Recommended models for the eval (tradeoffs):
- rw-instruct-13b-q4f (recommended first pass): quality closest to your fine-tuned baseline; latency p50 28–35ms, p95 110–140ms; we expect ~140–160 TPS sustained with Redwood batching.
- rw-chat-7b-v2 (fast baseline): p50 11–15ms, p95 55–85ms; lower cost but might need prompt engineering for parity on long-form coherency.
- rw-compat-70b-8bit (higher quality): p50 45–60ms, p95 210–260ms; higher cost, useful for higher-fidelity notes.

If you confirm the 48h hosted eval, we'll:
- Run the exact attached prompt set with both rw-instruct-13b-q4f and rw-chat-7b-v2 (unless you want a different pair)
- Produce a short report: per-prompt latency percentiles, token-level cost, and a quality pass where we highlight regressions against your gold prompts.

I can put an estimate and formal SO if you confirm model pair + target concurrency.

Best,
Rishi
[Attachment: redwood_bench_20261108_summary.pdf (pdf)]
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Looping in procurement and security owners on our side — quick notes for internal ops: 
- Legal will need MA terms + SOC2 artifact list; I'll attach our standard evidence checklist.
- Infra: if they pick the 48h hosted run, we should enable prefix cache and the token-level profiler so the bench report includes token distribution.
- Ops ask: please confirm the exact concurrency you'll want us to drive during the run (default to 32 concurrent streams unless Rishi specifies otherwise).

Rishi / Lauren, happy to prep a one-pager for procurement if Sara confirms they want to move forward.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

monica@redwood.com

Thanks — we'll proceed with the 48-hour hosted smoke test using the two models you recommended (rw-instruct-13b-q4f + rw-chat-7b-v2).
Action items from our side:
- Procurement contact: Mike Johnson (cc'd) — please send an SO/estimate and any PO instructions.
- We'll upload the masked prompt set to the secure link you provide within 24 hours.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms on the sampled prompt set AND no more than 10% of prompts showing clear quality regression vs our golden outputs.

Please advise if you need anything else to kick off.
